Caring for a Maltese Dog's Coat: From Bath to Blow Dry

A Maltese dog's long, silky white coat is one of its most striking features, but keeping it beautiful requires regular, thorough grooming sessions. Expect to set aside approximately 1.5 to 2.5 hours for the entire bathing, drying, and brushing process, depending on the length of your dog's coat and how cooperative your pup is.

1. Gather the correct products and tools. You will need a high-quality whitening or brightening shampoo (such as Chris Christensen White on White or Tropiclean Awapuhi White Shampoo), a moisturizing conditioner or detangling conditioner (such as The Stuff conditioner/detangler or Chris Christensen Ice on Ice), a leave-in conditioning spray, a pin brush with polished tips, a fine-toothed metal comb (a Greyhound-style comb works best), a slicker brush, a high-velocity pet dryer or a stand dryer, several absorbent towels, cotton balls for the ears, and a non-slip mat for the tub.

2. Pre-brush the coat thoroughly before the bath. Using your pin brush and metal comb, gently work through the entire coat from the ends upward to the skin, removing any existing tangles or small matts. Skipping this step will cause tangles to tighten and become much worse once the coat gets wet. Apply a light mist of leave-in detangling spray to stubborn spots to ease them out.

3. Prepare the bathing area and your dog. Place the non-slip mat in your sink or tub so your Maltese feels secure. Tuck a cotton ball gently into each ear to prevent water from entering the ear canals. Adjust the water temperature to lukewarm — neither hot nor cold — and thoroughly saturate the coat all the way down to the skin, which can take a few minutes given how dense a Maltese coat can be.

4. Apply the shampoo and wash the coat using proper technique. Dilute the shampoo slightly with water if the manufacturer recommends it, then work it through the coat in a downward, squeezing motion rather than scrubbing in circles. Circular scrubbing creates tangles and matts in the fine Maltese hair. Pay special attention to areas that get dirty fastest, such as the paws, belly, under the tail, and around the face. Use a tearless shampoo or a damp cloth for the face and around the eyes.

5. Rinse completely and repeat the shampoo if needed. Leftover shampoo residue will make the coat look dull, feel sticky, and attract dirt faster. Rinse until the water runs perfectly clear and you can feel the hair squeak slightly between your fingers. If your Maltese was particularly dirty, a second lather and rinse may be necessary.

6. Apply conditioner and allow it to penetrate the coat. Work a generous amount of moisturizing conditioner through the entire coat, again using a gentle squeezing motion from root to tip. Let the conditioner sit for three to five minutes so it can soften and protect the hair shafts. This step is critical for preventing tangles and breakage in the Maltese's fine, single-layer coat.

7. Rinse the conditioner thoroughly and gently remove excess water. Rinse until there is no slippery residue left, as leftover conditioner can weigh down the coat and cause it to look greasy. Once fully rinsed, use your hands to gently squeeze water from the coat in a downward motion. Avoid wringing or rubbing the hair, as this creates tangles. Remove the cotton balls from the ears.

8. Towel dry carefully using a patting and squeezing method. Wrap your Maltese in a highly absorbent microfiber towel and gently press and squeeze the coat to wick away moisture. Never rub the towel vigorously back and forth, as this roughs up the hair cuticle and causes matting. You may need two or three towels to remove as much water as possible before moving to the dryer.

9. Blow dry the coat on a low-heat or cool setting while brushing simultaneously. Using a high-velocity pet dryer or a stand dryer (which frees up both hands), dry the coat section by section. Start at the legs and work your way up the body. Hold the dryer at a slight angle and use your pin brush or slicker brush to gently brush through each section as the warm air passes over it. This technique straightens the coat, adds volume, and prevents tangles from forming as the hair dries. Never use high heat, as it can damage the fine Maltese hair and irritate the skin. This step alone can take 30 to 60 minutes.

10. Finish with a final comb-through and apply a leave-in conditioning spray. Once the coat is completely dry, use your fine-toothed metal comb to go through the entire coat one last time, checking for any remaining tangles or areas you may have missed. Lightly mist the coat with a leave-in conditioner or finishing spray to add shine, reduce static, and help protect against tangles between grooming sessions. Pay particular attention to areas prone to matting, such as behind the ears, under the legs, and around the collar area.

Maintaining a Maltese coat in top condition is a commitment, but following these steps consistently — ideally every one to two weeks — will keep the hair healthy, silky, and free of painful matts. With practice, the routine becomes smoother and faster, and your Maltese will look and feel their absolute best.
